findings.title: Access-token ID matcher does not check the grant shortcut
findings.body: This condition rejects a match when the extracted text equals the expected shortcut, and the substring range is also wrong: the grant shortcut occupies positions 4–5, not 3–4. As a result, the matcher accepts IDs with the wrong grant type and can reject IDs that contain the expected one, so the updated event assertions do not reliably verify grant encoding.

findings.title: Decoder assumes a two-character grant shortcut without enforcing it
findings.body: The decoder requires the encoded context to be exactly six characters, but `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` documents shortcuts as usually three letters, and the encoder concatenates the shortcut without validating its length. A grant provider returning a three-character shortcut can therefore issue an ID that this decoder rejects, making the encoder and decoder incompatible for a shortcut length the factory contract permits.
